title: Full integer state value function, re-run on the decided gate setup
question: Does experiment 13's result hold on the decided setup (3 opponents from the champions registry, the opponent model of #174): how well does a value function over the exact integer state predict the remaining score, and does the learned model or Monte Carlo predict better?
change: Experiment 13 unchanged except the setup: rl-gate's defaults (4 players, opponents greedy-full-probe, greedy-full-combo and the anchor greedy-full-probe shuffled per seed, engine of dev at 3fa9d33).
method: Training-set sizes 1k to 300k games (seeds 1..), 10,000 held-out games (seeds 500,000,000..), RMSE of the predicted remaining score
setups: Perfection, 16×16 continents, 4 players, Crazy, seat 0 Xin-Xi (human seat), learner greedy-full-probe; opponents greedy-full-probe, greedy-full-combo, greedy-full-probe (anchor), seats shuffled per seed (rl-gate defaults)

headline.label: Held-out RMSE of remaining score, 300k training games: turn baseline vs model-based V
